newsitem.title: SWEDEN: SWIMMING-CLAUDIA POLL IS AN EARLY BIRD.
newsitem.headline: SWIMMING-CLAUDIA POLL IS AN EARLY BIRD.

text.p: Rising every day at 0300 and training until 0600 in a chilly pool is Costa Rican Claudia Poll's recipe for international swimming success.
The 24-year-old Atlanta Olympic gold medallist set a world record for the women's 200 metres freestyle on Friday, the second day of the world short-course swimming championships.

"I knew about two weeks ago that I could do it. I was doing under two minutes in practice. My coach knew it in February but I didn't believe him right away," she told a news conference after paring the previous record of one minute 55.42 seconds down to 1:54.17.
A hard worker who loves competition, she follows a training schedule that would make many blanche.
"I wake up at three o'clock in the morning and train from 3.30 until 6.00, and then I go to the university and then come back from 3.30 to 6.30 in the afternoon," she said.

"It gets pretty cold, 16 degrees (C) or 17 degrees. Although it's a tropical country, it's very windy where the pool is, so in the morning it gets very cold. But my coach tells me it's not really cold, it's in my mind."
Neither Poll nor coach Francisco Rivas would predict her chances of breaking another record when she swims in Saturday's 400 metres freestyle.
"I'll see tomorrow morning, when I wake up, how my body responds to doing 1:54.17," Poll said, adding that she would be looking to try other events in the future.
"It's pretty hard to break 1:54.17, so maybe we'll switch to another stroke or the individual medley to reach new goals."
Her next competition is in Monaco next month.
